messages:
maria (eng-platform): heads-up — p95 for /v1/generate in eu-west jumped ~120ms -> ~420ms around 03/18. dashboard shows endpoint p50/p95/p99. weirdly, if i add the HTTP method slice (GET vs POST) the p95 gap vanishes. anyone seen http_method affect percentile merges like this?

alex (metric-systems): yeah — this smells like how we roll up sampled histograms. when you merge cohorts with very different sample distributions (payloads, queue times) the resulting p95 can shift if sample weights/counts or tags aren't preserved. do you have a quick repro?

maria (eng-platform): i grabbed the console view and then ran a raw query on the telemetry index. quick snippet of what i ran:

```
# results from kq (simplified)
group_by: [endpoint, region]
query_filter: endpoint = "/v1/generate" and region = "eu-west"
sample_source: ingest-raw
rollup: tdigest
```

when group_by includes http_method the p95 for POST is ~410ms and GET ~90ms. when method is omitted merged p95 is ~420ms (so dominated by POST) but the UI showed a step-change which confused the product team.

sam (ingest): confirmed on my side — POSTs have much larger payloads + KV cache misses -> higher tail. our sampling config used to drop the http_method tag during ingestion for a couple of rollup paths to save cardinality. that would explain the disappearance of the slice in the merged view.

donna (product): product question — user-facing alert fired on the endpoint-level p95 spike. if the spike is just POSTs, we can scope alerts differently. what's lower-effort: change alerting or change rollup to keep method?

alex (metric-systems): options, trade-offs: preserve http_method in the rollup keys for that endpoint (accurate but raises cardinality + storage/cost), or keep rollups as-is but change dashboard defaults / alerts to include method breakdown for generate endpoints. there's also a middle ground: only preserve method for POST for endpoints with high variance.

maria (eng-platform): agree. i'm worried about developers getting false regressions when a rollout changes POST traffic. is there a quick mitigation we can do in console UX so alerts don't trigger on merged percentiles if cohort variance is high? maybe display a sample-entropy or a "mixed-cohorts" badge?

alex (metric-systems): we can compute a tiny heuristic at query time: if the inter-cohort p95 spread > 20% and the dominant cohort weight < 80%, show a yellow badge: "percentile sensitive to cohort mixing". cheap to compute from existing t-digest metadata (count per subgroup).

sam (ingest): quick engineering fix: i can flip a sampling-config for /v1/generate to preserve http_method in the tdigest rollup for eu-west. low-risk; increases cardinality only for that route. infra-bot will record rollout.

infra-bot: deploy: sampling-config-change applied for route=/v1/generate scope=region:eu-west keep_tags=[http_method] rollout=canary(5%) -> 100% started by sam at 2026-03-19T14:20Z :rocket:

maria (eng-platform): awesome, thanks. i'll re-query after canary completes and flag the dashboards that fired alerts. can someone add the badge suggestion to the metrics UX backlog?
donna (product): added: https://linear.app/RW/issue/PLATFORM-674 percentiles-badge-for-cohort-mixing (small UX + metric check)

alex (metric-systems): follow-up note: longer-term we should document that endpoint-level percentiles can be misleading when method/payload varies. maybe add a short help tooltip in the console: "Tip: enable additional slices (http_method, client_type) to verify percentile provenance."

maria (eng-platform): agreed. i'll keep an eye for 1h and post results. thanks all. :thumbsup:
